title: 1952 Egyptian revolution
summary: On 23 July 1952 the Free Officers, led by Col. Gamal Abdel Nasser, toppled Egypt's monarchy in a coup. Scholars describe it as a coup that preempted a revolution. Free Officers rule shaped Egypt for decades, and the coup is often cited as a case of coup contagion in the Middle East.

reviewer_note: Sources are a Britannica section on Egypt and a journal article treating the coup as a case study; the article does not give the date itself. Britannica mentions Farouk only in a caption and says the republic was declared in July 1952 there, but Egypt officially became a republic in June 1953 in the text. Not reconciled here. Place is the whole country. Summary uses Britannica for the date. Importance judgement is mine. Nothing else was stretched. Minor tension noted. Revolution vs coup terminology varies.
